children: Feature Explores the Real Biology Behind Recombinant Spider Silk and the Scientific Case for Kraig Labs' Production Platform
ANN ARBOR, Mich., Sept. 03, 2026
-- Kraig Biocraft Laboratories, Inc.
OTCQB:KBLB
("the Company", "Kraig Labs", or "Kraig's"), a world leader in spider silk technology*, today highlighted recent coverage by
examining the scientific gap between fictional biology and real-world advances in recombinant spider silk production.
The August 31, 2026 Tech Times feature,

params.linkText: Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s Silk Is Commercially Real; Wrist Location Breaks Biology

children: , by Philip Nickell, takes a detailed look at the biology underlying spider silk. It connects popular culture's take on biological innovation to the real scientific and commercialization work underway today.

This in-depth article addresses a central element in commercializing spider silk. Producing spider silk proteins is only the first step. Engineering a practical biological system that can produce silk at scale is the key driver for broad commercialization. Rather than recreating a spider's silk-producing anatomy from scratch, Kraig Labs uses the naturally evolved silk-producing machinery of the silkworm. Genetic engineering introduces key spider silk proteins into that existing biological platform.

As the article notes, Kraig Labs uses genetically engineered Bombyx mori silkworms as biological production systems. This model leverages the silkworms' sophisticated silk glands and spinning architecture.

That distinct strategy sits at the core of Kraig Labs' technology. The challenge was never proving that spider silk proteins can be produced. It was building a production platform that delivers recombinant spider silk at meaningful scale, with commercially relevant properties.

Kraig Labs recently reported strong progress on that front. On August 24, 2026, the Company announced a new production record, increasing output more than 30% above its previous milestone. The achievement stood out for another reason. It came during the rainy season, one of the most technically demanding stretches of the Company's production calendar.

The Tech Times feature offers a compelling lens on that progress. By explaining why fictional wrist spinnerets are biologically implausible, and how transgenic silkworms offer a scientifically credible path to commercial spider silk production. The article places Kraig Labs' technology within the broader history of spider silk research and its leading role in its commercialization.

“We appreciate Tech Times for bringing this level of scientific depth to the conversation around spider silk. This article captures exactly what we set out to build,” said Kim Thompson, Founder and CEO of Kraig Biocraft Laboratories. “We took a proven biological system and gave it a new purpose. That work is now producing real silk, at real scale, moving toward real commercial applications.”

Thompson added, "The distinction between producing spider silk proteins and reproducing the biological machinery that spins them is exactly what our technology does. This article highlights what we’ve known all along; the key to unlocking spider silk's commercial potential was a cost-effective and scalable production platform.”

Kraig Labs' technology is built around a genetically engineered silkworm that produces recombinant spider silk. From single grams to metric tons, the Company has turned a scientific breakthrough into a functioning production platform.
